meta_description: Scuba diving in Dubai from €86: no-certificate first dives, Deep Dive Dubai's 60 m pool and Fujairah reef trips compared on depth, transfer and price.

lead: Never dived? Book the €86 Discover Scuba dive at Jumeirah Beach: 3 hours, down to 12 metres in the open sea, deeper than the €173 private dive that costs twice as much. Already certified? Go east: 2 guided reef dives in Fujairah cost €148 with hotel transfer, €74 a dive, against €296 for a single dive at Deep Dive Dubai.

Two questions decide the rest. Do you have a certificate, and do you want the pool or the open sea? Deep Dive Dubai is the world's deepest pool, 2 hours in the city with a sunken set and no fish. Fujairah on the east coast means coral, wrecks and turtles, but a 6:00 AM pickup, an 8-hour day and on two trips an AED 160 transfer fee that is not in the headline price.
Below are the 8 best options, from €86 sea dives to Deep Dive Dubai's 30-metre guided dive, plus snorkelling picks for non-divers. Use the filters to see only beginner, certified, pool or sea trips.

review: This is the sensible default for anyone who types "scuba diving Dubai" and has never dived. For €86 you get a 3-hour session with skills training, then a guided descent off Jumeirah Beach to a maximum of 12 metres. That depth matters: the pool and private options on this page stop at 4 m (Sunken City Walk) or 6–8 m (VIP private dive), so you get a deeper first dive for less money.

Compared with the Fujairah day trips at €107, you save €21 on the listed price, skip the AED 160 transfer fee those trips add, and avoid a 6:00 AM pickup. The trade-off is the setting: the east coast sells coral gardens and turtles, while this is a city-side dive. If your priority is simply breathing underwater for the first time, this one does it in a morning.

Equipment and instruction are included, and you meet at the centre at Azure Residences on Palm Jumeirah, handy if you are staying nearby. Hotel pickup is not part of the package, so sort out your own taxi. You cannot fly on the same day after diving, so do not book it for your departure day.

The boat goes out from Dibba in Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, the instructor takes you on a try dive to up to 10 metres, and then you swap to snorkel gear to swim with sea turtles. It is the same €107 listed price as the other Fujairah beginner trip (#5) but rated 4.9 and includes snacks on board.

Do the real maths before booking: €107 plus AED 160 for the return transfer, which is paid on arrival. That makes it the most expensive beginner sea dive after the VIP private option, and the day takes about 8 hours. Per hour it is still good value, and you get two activities, but it is not a quick add-on.
Two rules catch people out: you must be able to swim, and you must present your original passport. Non-swimmers should look at the VIP private dive (#6) or the Sunken City Walk (#7) instead.

review: This is the dive behind most "deep dive Dubai" searches from divers. You get one guided dive in a 60-metre indoor pool with a flooded city to explore, and the depth is set by your card: open-water divers stay shallow, advanced divers can go to 30 metres. Entry, equipment, gases and a dive guide are included, and the whole thing takes about 2 hours. You make your own way to NAS Sports Complex.

At €296 it costs twice the Fujairah 2-dive trip (#4, €148 for two dives, so €74 per dive against €296 here). You are paying for the setting, the visibility and the convenience of not leaving Dubai, not for marine life. Book it for the novelty, and book the east coast if you want fish.

It is non-refundable, so lock it in only once your dates are fixed. Plan the rest of the day too: you must avoid flying or high altitude, Burj Khalifa included, for at least 12 hours after a single dive (18 hours after more than one), so book your Burj Khalifa tickets for an earlier day.

guide.h2: Dubai Scuba Diving Compared: Certificate, Pool vs Sea, Price
guide.html:
The two questions that decide your booking: do you hold a dive certificate, and do you want the open sea or the pool. Here are all 8 options on those axes, with the real cost once transfer fees are added.

OptionCertificateWhereUnderwaterTrip timeTransferPrice
#1 Discover Scuba, Jumeirah BeachNot neededSea, Dubai1 dive, up to 12 m3 hMeet at centre€86
#2 Discovery Scuba & Snorkel, DibbaNot needed, must swimSea, Fujairah1 try dive, up to 10 m + snorkel8 hAED 160 extra€107 + AED 160
#3 Deep Dive guided diveRequiredPool, Dubai1 dive, 10/18/30 m2 hOwn way€296
#4 2 dives for certified diversRequiredSea, Fujairah2 dives, 2 sites8 hIncluded€148 (€74/dive)
#5 Fujairah dive + snorkelBoth tracksSea, FujairahBeginners 1 dive, certified 28 hAED 160 extra€107 + AED 160
#6 VIP private diveNot needed, no swimmingSea, Dubai30–45 min, 6–8 m3 hIncluded€173
#7 Sunken City WalkNot needed, no swimmingPool, Dubai30 min session at 4 m1.5 hOwn way€148 (≈€4.90/min)
#8 Deep Dive snorkellingNot needed, must swimPool, DubaiSurface snorkel, 1 h1 hOwn way€99

What the numbers show: the cheapest real dive is #1 at €86, and it goes deeper (12 m) than both the private dive (6–8 m) and the Sunken City Walk (4 m). For certified divers, the Fujairah 2-dive trip works out at €74 per dive with transfer included, a quarter of the per-dive cost of Deep Dive Dubai (€296 for one dive). Both €107 Fujairah beginner trips cost more than they look, because the AED 160 return transfer is paid on arrival.

• Never dived, want it quick and cheap: #1 Discover Scuba at Jumeirah Beach. €86, 3 hours, up to 12 m, meet at the centre on Palm Jumeirah.
  • Never dived, want reefs and turtles: #2 Discovery Scuba & Snorkelling in Dibba. Budget a full day and AED 160 for the transfer.
  • Can't swim or very nervous: #6 VIP private dive for a real sea dive with your own instructor, or #7 Sunken City Walk to stand 4 m down inside Deep Dive Dubai.
  • Certified, want the best dives for the money: #4 2 dives in Fujairah, €74 per dive with hotel transfer.
  • Certified, want the dive nobody else offers: #3 Deep Dive Dubai guided dive, up to 30 m in the world's deepest pool, 2 hours, no early start.
  • One certified diver plus one beginner: #5 Fujairah dive + snorkel, both on the same boat.
  • Family with kids aged 6–11: #8 Deep Dive snorkelling. The Fujairah half-day trip (#5) starts at 12, and the Deep Dive dive and walk at 10.

Pool or sea? Pick the pool (Deep Dive Dubai) for guaranteed visibility, a short city-based slot and something no other dive site has. Pick the sea for marine life: Jumeirah Beach for a short first dive, Fujairah on the east coast (roughly 2 hours by road each way) for coral, wrecks and turtles.

guide.h2: Snorkelling in Dubai: Pool or Sea
guide.html:
If nobody in your group wants a tank on their back, there are two snorkelling routes:

  • Pool snorkelling at Deep Dive Dubai (#8, €99, 1 hour, ages 6+): surface snorkel over the sunken city with a guide and life jacket. Good for kids, no marine life.
  • Sea snorkelling in Fujairah: both east coast beginner trips (#2 and #5) include snorkelling gear, and #2 specifically snorkels where sea turtles feed. You book the dive trip, so it is a full day, but you get the dive and the snorkel for one price.

Want more time on the water instead? Compare jet ski tours in Dubai or our wider Dubai adrenaline experiences.

guide.h2: Before You Book: Flying, Documents and Extra Costs
guide.html:
• No flying, no Burj Khalifa straight after. Deep Dive Dubai asks you to avoid flying or high altitude for 12 hours after one dive and 18 hours after more than one, the Fujairah half-day trip says wait 18 hours before flying, and the Jumeirah Beach dive says no flying on the same day. Dive early in your trip and schedule your Burj Khalifa visit helicopter or balloon flights on another day.
  • Passport: the Fujairah trips (#2, #4) ask for your original passport; most other listings ask for a passport or ID card.
  • Certification card: certified-only options (#3, #4) need your licence or a photo of it (Deep Dive Dubai accepts an image).
  • Waivers: all three Deep Dive Dubai options require an online waiver before the visit, and no alcohol or non-prescription drugs for 24 hours before.
  • What costs extra: the AED 160 return transfer on #2 and #5, paid on arrival. Underwater photos are included only on #6; Deep Dive Dubai sells video and facility-tour upgrades.
  • Early starts: Fujairah pickups are between 6:00 and 7:00 AM. You are back by early afternoon, so an evening desert safari fits the same day better than the night before.
  • Bring: swimwear and a towel for every option (towels are supplied on #6).
  • Cancellation: the five sea options have free cancellation up to 24 hours before; the three Deep Dive Dubai tickets are non-refundable.

faqs.q: How much does scuba diving in Dubai cost?
faqs.a: A first dive in the sea starts at €86 per person (3 hours at Jumeirah Beach). East coast beginner trips to Fujairah are €107 plus AED 160 for the return transfer. Certified divers pay €148 for 2 guided dives with transfer in Fujairah, or €296 for one guided dive at Deep Dive Dubai.

faqs.q: Can I scuba dive in Dubai without a certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. The Discover Scuba dive at Jumeirah Beach (€86), the VIP private dive (€173) and both Fujairah beginner trips (€107) need no certificate. The VIP private dive and the Deep Dive Sunken City Walk do not even require you to swim.

faqs.q: How much is Deep Dive Dubai?
faqs.a: For certified divers, a guided dive including entry, equipment and gases costs from €296. Non-divers can do the 30-minute Sunken City Walk for €148 or 1 hour of surface snorkelling for €99. All three are non-refundable.

faqs.q: Is diving better in Dubai or Fujairah?
faqs.a: For marine life, Fujairah. The east coast trips dive coral gardens, wrecks and reefs with turtles and reef fish, but take about 8 hours with a 6:00–7:00 AM pickup. Dubai is better for a short first dive (Jumeirah Beach, 3 hours) or for the Deep Dive Dubai pool.

faqs.q: What is the minimum age for scuba diving in Dubai?
faqs.a: On this shortlist, 10 for Deep Dive Dubai's guided dive and Sunken City Walk, and 12 for the Fujairah half-day dive and snorkel trip. Children from 6 can join the Deep Dive Dubai snorkelling session.

faqs.q: Where can I go snorkeling in Dubai?
faqs.a: At Deep Dive Dubai's pool (€99, 1 hour, ages 6+) or on the Fujairah beginner dive trips, which include snorkelling with reef fish and sea turtles after the dive.

faqs.q: Can I go up the Burj Khalifa after diving?
faqs.a: Not on the same day. Deep Dive Dubai asks you to wait at least 12 hours after a single dive (18 hours after more than one) before flying or going to high altitude, the Burj Khalifa included. Book your Burj Khalifa tickets for a different day.

methodology: We compared 8 of Dubai's most popular scuba and snorkelling experiences side by side: no-certificate try dives, certified-diver trips, Deep Dive Dubai's pool and Fujairah east coast boats. Each was scored on certification needed, pool or sea, depth or time underwater, total trip time, transfer and the full price including transfer fees, using live listing prices for a normal date. Price per dive and per minute underwater were calculated where depth or time underwater is stated.
